name: Lukey
tagline: Not a leak. THE leaks. Plural. He's a franchise.

romance_success.title: Head Over Heels Over Pipes
romance_success.text: Lukey stayed. He's dry, he's solid, his hair is ENORMOUS and he is absolutely gone on you. He still floods Dan's shoes every Friday. Out of love.

romance_failure.title: Love You to the Last Drop
romance_failure.text: He loved you enough to go. All that's left is a heart-shaped drop on the kitchen floor that never quite dries. You'd never mop it anyway.

friend_success.title: Pipe Dreams Come True
friend_success.text: Lukey finally got his date (a 'frate,' technically), finished his business and passed on in a cloud of hairspray. Brenda would be proud. Probably.

friend_failure.title: Fixed It Myself (Mostly)
friend_failure.text: Lukey passed on a little grumpy, a lot proud and fully convinced he did all the work. ('You held the torch.') The house is dry. Dan's shoes are dry. Everyone's dry. Nobody's thrilled.

lines: *A gush of water bursts from under the sink. A very damp man with a magnificent mullet slides out on a wave, like he's been rehearsing this entrance for years.*
Easy, easy. I know. It's a lot of leak to take in.
Name's Lukey. I'm the leaks around here. Not A leak. THE leaks. Plural. I'm a [franchise].

choices.text: You're a leak? You don't look like a leak.
You're cute. For a water stain.
Great. So you're the thing I'm here to fix.

lines: Kitchen sink? Me. Bathroom ceiling? Me. That damp patch on the east wall that looks like Elvis? VERY much me.
I've got locations all over this house, babe. I'm basically a chain restaurant. But wetter.

choices.text: You're a leak? You don't look like a leak.
A franchise. Cute. For a water stain.
So I'm closing down every branch. Got it.

lines: Thank you. I moisturize. Constantly. Involuntarily.
*He flicks his hair. It sprays the toaster.*
*Drip-drip-drip-drip.*
Okay, wow. Bold opener. I respect it. Most people open with a mop.
For the record, I'm not a stain. Stains are passive. I'm a FEATURE.
Fix? FIX? Wow. First date and you're already trying to change me.
*A jet of water hits you square in the chest.*
Oops. Pressure's a bit high today. Wonder why.
So, new girl. Want the tour of my empire?
Kitchen sink, that's headquarters. Bathroom ceiling, that's the penthouse. East wall, summer home.
And the radiator in the hall? Holiday home. Very exclusive. Just me and a dead moth called Gerald.

choices.text: The bathroom CEILING? Have you been watching me shower?
Honestly? That's an impressive property portfolio.
And every single one of those is getting patched.

lines: *He goes very, very still. A single drop falls from the ceiling in the next room.*
I have NEVER looked. I look at the GROUT. Respectfully. Like a gentleman.
...Nice shampoo, though. Coconut?
THANK you. Finally, a woman who appreciates real estate.
I'm basically a property mogul. All my properties are damp. And technically yours. But still.
Patched? ALL of them? Even the summer home?
*Somewhere in the east wall, something drips sadly.*
That's cold. That's cold water, new girl. And I would know.
Here's the thing, though. Every leak you patch... that's a bit of me gone.
You fix the bathroom, I lose the penthouse. You fix the sink, I lose the whole operation.
I'm not being dramatic. I'm being DAMP.

choices.text: Then I'll go slow. Gently. I promise.
Maybe we can figure this out together.
Should've thought of that before you wrecked my drywall.

lines: *The dripping slows to something almost shy.*
...Gently. Okay. Nobody's ever said 'gently' to me. Usually it's 'call a plumber' and a lot of screaming.
*Lukey will remember that.*
Together? Like a team? Like a buddy cop show? 'Leak and Flipper'?
I'd watch that. I'd be the handsome one.
*Lukey will remember that.*
Your drywall was LOVING it. Your drywall has never felt so alive.
*Every tap in the kitchen turns on at once.*
That was me. Just so we're clear. I'm very powerful.
Also, who was the windbreaker this morning? Clipboard. Moustache. Said your foundation had 'great bones.'
GREAT BONES. That's flirting. That's building-code flirting.

choices.text: That's Inspector Dan. He comes every Friday.
Are you jealous of a building inspector?
He's actually kind of charming.

lines: Every FRIDAY? Like a standing date?
Right. Fine. Good. I'll be ready. I'll be very damp and very intimidating.
Jealous? Of DAN? A man who owns a windbreaker on PURPOSE?
*Drip. Drip. Dripdripdripdrip.*
...Is it working? The windbreaker? Asking for a leak.
CHARMING? His pun was 'Sounds like you've got a leak-ing problem.' That's not a pun. That's barely a WORD.
I'm going to pun that man into the ground. Friday. It's on.
*He glares across the kitchen at your brand-new dishwasher.*
And who's the new guy?

choices.text: That's the dishwasher. Be nice.
Your replacement. He's very discreet.
Relax. He's not my type. Too many buttons.

lines: Nice? He uses water like he OWNS it. Some of us were here first, mate.
Discreet? He BEEPS. Every time he finishes, he BEEPS. Who does that?
*The dishwasher beeps. Lukey hisses at it.*
Too many buttons. Ha. Yeah. You want a simpler model. One button. Very damp.
*He winks. It's mostly a drip.*
*You hold out your hand to shake on a truce. It goes straight through him. It's like shaking hands with a sprinkler.*
Ooh. Cold. Sorry. There's not much of me in any one place. I'm spread a bit thin.
Fine. Fix the bathroom first, if you have to. Never liked the penthouse. Terrible acoustics.
...Be gentle with my ceiling, new girl.
You WERE gentle with the bathroom. I noticed. I barely felt a thing.
Well. I felt a bit. Nice hands. Moving on.
Oh. It's you. The woman who murdered my penthouse. I've been in mourning. I've been dripping in black.
...Fine. Truce. I'm bored.
*There's a new damp patch on the kitchen wall. It's shaped like a heart. It gets bigger when you walk in.*
Afternoon, boss. You patched the bathroom. I can't feel my left side.
Also, those podcast ladies think there's a giant [catfish] living in the walls. I'm not a catfish. ...Am I a catfish?
I'm not wet in a fish way. I'm wet in a SEXY way.

choices.text: Definitely the sexy way.
Lukey, you're the least fish-like thing I've ever met.
Can we talk about the heart-shaped damp patch?

lines: Also, apparently someone's being CATFISHED? Trish thinks it's you. Who's texting you at two in the morning?
...Is it Dan? It's Dan, isn't it. He's got catfish energy. All moustache, no fins.
*The heart-shaped damp patch gets significantly bigger.*
That's— okay. That's just condensation. It's humid. Shut up.
Thank you. I have no scales. I have ABS. I think. It's hard to tell, I'm mostly drip.
What heart? That's not a heart. That's a very romantic stain. Walls do that. Coincidence.
*It throbs. Slightly.*
Anyway. You're doing the east wall next. My SUMMER HOME. I'd like it on record that I object.
But if you're going in, you need me. I know every drip in that wall. I've lived there since 1986. Er— since forever. Since INSTALLATION.
*He's humming 'Livin' on a Prayer' while he says it.*

choices.text: Lukey, how does a leak know Bon Jovi?
Since 1986? That's weirdly specific.
Fine. Show me where. I'll take the help.

lines: Everyone knows Bon Jovi. It's in the water. Literally. I'm the water.
*He does a small, completely unconscious Running Man.*
Leaks dance. It's a known thing. Look it up.
Is it? Big year for leaks. Excellent vintage. Shoulder pads were huge. For pipes. Pipe shoulder pads.
...Leave it.
Oh, NOW she wants my help. When it's my summer home on the line.
...Second stud from the left. Mind the wire. And the wasp nest. That's Kevin. Kevin's harmless.
*You open the east wall together. He talks you through every drip, pointing with a wet finger, very close to your ear.*
*It is the most romantic plumbing you have ever done.*
*When you're done, the summer home is dry, and Lukey looks noticeably more THERE. Less drizzle, more man.*
Huh. Fewer leaks, less of me spread around. I feel... concentrated. Like an orange juice.

choices.text: You look good concentrated.
Does it hurt? Losing a leak?
Great. Two down, two to go.

lines: *He checks his reflection in the toaster. He likes what he sees.*
I DO look good. Wow. Has this jawline been here the whole time?
Nah. It tickles. Like losing a sock. Except the sock is your summer home.
...Thanks for asking, though. Nobody ever asks the leaks how they're doing.
Wow. Counting down. Like New Year's Eve. Except at midnight I'm gone and you get drywall.
*A slow, sarcastic drip.*
*Friday. Inspector Dan admires the east wall. 'Nice work. Water-tight. Much like my alibi.' He chuckles at his own joke, then invites you for coffee to 'discuss permits.'*
*From inside the wall, a small but furious gurgle.*
*When Dan leaves, both of his shoes are full of water. Somehow.*

choices.text: Lukey! Did you flood Dan's shoes?
You're cute when you're jealous.
It's just coffee. About permits.

lines: Flood is a strong word. I'd say 'refreshed.' His feet looked hot.
He said 'water-tight like my alibi,' boss. That's a crime against puns. I was punishing a crime.
Jealous? Me? Of a man who wears a windbreaker INDOORS?
*The heart-shaped damp patch is now the size of a door.*
...Okay. Maybe a bit. You're not supposed to fancy the leaks, you know. It's against code. Dan would write you up.
'Permits.' Sure. That's what they're calling it now. In my day it was 'grabbing a milkshake.'
*He freezes.*
In my day? What day? Leaks don't have days. Forget I said that.
Right. The radiator's next, isn't it? My holiday home. Gerald's going to be devastated.
Save the kitchen for last, yeah? That's where most of me is.
And boss? This was nice. The wall thing. With you. Strictly professional, obviously.

choices.text: It was NOT strictly professional.
Good work today, partner.
Stay out of Dan's shoes.

lines: *Every tap in the kitchen turns on, then off, then on again. It's either a malfunction or a standing ovation.*
Professionally speaking? Agreed. Goodnight, boss.
Partner. 'Leak and Flipper.' I'm getting us matching jackets. Mine will be damp.
Night, boss.
No promises. Those shoes are basically a paddling pool with laces. It'd be rude NOT to.
*A cheeky drip. Then silence.*
*The power's out across the block. The kitchen is lit by candles and the soft blue shimmer of the last leak in the house.*
You did the radiator. My holiday home. I'm a one-bedroom now, boss. One sink. Just me and the U-bend.
*He's more solid than ever. In the candlelight he's mostly man and only a little bit puddle.*
So. Blackout. Candles. You, me and a box of pasta. This isn't a date.

choices.text: It's definitely a date.
It's a working dinner. Between colleagues.
It's a power cut, Lukey. Calm down.

lines: *The tap turns on by itself, then off again. Flustered.*
Okay. It's a date. Fine. I'm not nervous. I'm just very... runny tonight.
I'm going to call you sweetheart now. I've decided. Sweetheart. There. Done. Moving on.
Colleagues. Right. Very professional. Two professionals. In candlelight. Sharing spaghetti.
I'm going to call you sweetheart, though. Professionally.
I AM calm. I am a calm, still body of water.
*A small wave crosses the sink.*
...Mostly still. Pass the parmesan, sweetheart.
*He 'cooks' by filling the pot from across the room with surgical precision and giving you terrible advice about salt.*
Did you hear the podcast? Mrs. Pruitt next door says someone's been singing [Bon Jovi|bonjovi] in the walls at night.
Ridiculous. I don't sing. I RESONATE.

choices.text: Sing for me.
Lukey... do you ever wonder why you know all this 80s stuff?
You definitely sing. You're terrible.

lines: *He hums the first line of 'Livin' on a Prayer.' Then the second. Then he's doing the guitar solo with a ladle.*
Okay. Maybe I resonate a LOT.
*He sings 'Livin' on a Prayer' into a wooden spoon. He hits none of the notes. He commits completely.*
*When he gets to 'take my hand,' he holds his out.*
Wonder? Why would I wonder? Leaks absorb culture. Through the walls. Like a sponge. A very cultured sponge.
*He goes quiet for a second.*
...Sometimes I dream about leg warmers. Is that normal for plumbing?
TERRIBLE? I'm a SOPRANO, sweetheart. You just can't hear it over the dripping.
*He sings a single, very high note. A wine glass cracks. He looks delighted.*
*He's reaching for you across the counter. There's only one leak left in the house now, so there's finally enough of him in one place.*
*His hand doesn't pass through yours. It's cool, a little damp and very definitely a hand.*
...Oh. Hello.

choices.text: Hold on to it.
Lukey! You're solid!
Your hand is clammy.

lines: *He does. Neither of you says anything for a while. The candles flicker. The last leak drips, very slowly, very happily.*
First thing I've held in years that wasn't a U-bend. Bit of an upgrade, sweetheart.
Mostly solid! Like a jelly! A handsome jelly!
*He squeezes your hand, then pokes his own face to check.*
I'm a LEAK. What did you expect, a hand cream advert?
*But he doesn't let go.*
*The radio crackles back to life. 'BIG STORM SATURDAY. Heavy rain and flooding expected.'*
*Every candle flame in the room shivers. So does Lukey.*
Flooding. I don't like flooding. For leak reasons. Very normal leak reasons.

choices.text: Whatever happens, we'll handle it together.
A leak that's scared of floods? That's like a fish scared of the sea.
It's just rain. Pull yourself together.

lines: Together. Yeah. Leak and Flipper. Season finale. Big storm episode.
*He squeezes your hand. He's still holding it. He forgot to let go. He's not going to.*
Don't. Don't bring fish into this. Bev's already got me down as a catfish.
...But yeah. Weird, right? Something about it makes my mullet stand up.
I AM together. I'm the most together I've been in years. Literally. I'm down to one sink.
*Drip. Sulky drip.*
*Friday. Dan peers under the sink. 'Last leak in the house? You're really draining the competition.' He waits for a laugh.*
*Behind him, letters appear in the condensation on the kitchen window: 'DRAIN-ING? WEAK. -L'*

choices.text: Lukey, stop writing on my windows.
Hit him with a better one.
Honestly, Dan's pun was better.

lines: It's not writing, it's COMMUNICATION. The window's basically my phone.
*The window fogs up again: 'sorry x'*
*The window fogs up: 'DAN. YOUR PUNS ARE A PIPE DREAM. YOU'RE ALL WASHED UP. GO WITH THE FLOW, MATE.'*
*Dan reads it, looks at you, slowly lowers his clipboard and leaves without a word.*
I WON. Did you see that? Sweetheart, I won the Friday.
*The window fogs up with a single, devastated word: 'WOW.'*
*A drip runs down the glass like a tear. It's a bit much. It's working, though.*
*Late. The candles are stubs. He's sitting on the counter, swinging his very solid legs.*
Sweetheart... I don't really know what I am. A leak. A bunch of leaks. One leak now. Whatever.
But I like who I am when you're here.
*A beat.*
That's the only soppy thing I'm saying this month. Goodnight. Don't patch me in your sleep.
*Saturday morning. Storm clouds over Heartbreak Lane. Lukey is sitting on the kitchen floor, very still, very solid and very pale.*
{player}.
*It's the first time he's ever used your real name. It sounds good in his mouth. He looks like he's been practicing.*
{player}, did you listen to the podcast?
*Saturday morning. Storm clouds over Heartbreak Lane. Lukey is sitting on the kitchen floor, very still, very solid and very pale.*
Sweetheart. Did you listen to the podcast?
'Local aerobics instructor Luke Moretti, 34, died in 1987 while attempting to repair a sink on a first date.'
That's me. I'm not a leak. I'm a GUY. I'm a guy who died SHOWING OFF.
I told her I was great with my hands. Her name was Brenda. She went to get the wine, I went under the sink, I slipped on the puddle and I bonked my head on the U-bend.
*He puts his face in his hands. They're very solid hands now.*
I died in LYCRA, sweetheart. In front of BRENDA.

choices.text: For what it's worth, I bet you looked great in Lycra.
Lukey. You're a PERSON. That's huge.
Laugh. You can't help it.

lines: *He peeks through his fingers.*
...I did look great. Legs like a racehorse. Shiny. Teal.
I know. I KNOW. I have a birthday! I have a star sign! I'm probably a Leo.
I'm DEFINITELY a Leo.
Oh, laugh it up. It IS hilarious. 'Man dies trying to impress woman with plumbing.' It's a Darwin Award with a mullet.
*He's laughing too. A bit. Despite himself.*
And the worst part? I never got the date. Brenda came back with the wine, and I was... busy. Being dead.
Thirty-nine years of dripping, and I think that's it. That's why I'm still here. I never got my date.

choices.text: Then let's fix this sink, and I'll take you on that date.
We'll get you your date. Even if it's just as friends.
Can we focus on the sink? The storm's here.

lines: *The last leak goes drip-drip-drip-drip so fast it's basically a tap.*
A date. With you. Okay. YES. Brenda who? I mean— bless Brenda. Lovely woman. Anyway. YES.
A friend date. A FRATE. Yeah. I'd like that. No pressure. Some pressure. I'm water, everything's pressure.
Right. Sink. Storm. The exact thing that killed me. No pressure.
*The storm hits. Rain hammers the windows. The kitchen sink, the last leak, the one that started it all, groans, shudders and sprays.*
Okay! This is it! Righty-tighty! Lefty-loosey is how I DIED!
*You get under the sink together. He can't hold the wrench, but he knows every inch of that pipe. You're his hands. He's your eyes. Nobody is slipping today.*

choices.text: Talk me through it, instructor.
I trust you. Show me.
Step back. I've got this.

lines: INSTRUCTOR. Okay! Quarter turn! And REACH! And TWIST! Feel the burn! Engage your core!
That last bit's aerobics. Ignore it. Actually don't, your core looks great.
*He puts his hands over yours on the wrench. Bolt by bolt. His voice is steady and soft the whole time.*
There. Feel that? That's the last one. You did it, sweetheart.
*You do it yourself. It takes three tries and a lot of swearing. He hovers, hands half-raised, not quite helping.*
...You held the wrench right. I'll give you that.
*Thunk. Squeak. Silence.*
*Outside, the storm rages. Inside, for the first time in thirty-nine years, there isn't a single leak in the house.*
*Lukey looks down at himself. Not one drop. And his hair, for the first time since 1987, is DRY. It's enormous.*
...Oh my god. The VOLUME. Sweetheart, look at the volume.
*Monday. The storm has passed. Inspector Dan signs off on every pipe in the house and leaves, deeply confused about why his shoes are dry for once.*
*That night you set the table. Candles. Wine. Bon Jovi on the stereo. Lukey is wearing a blazer he has somehow summoned from 1987. Its shoulder pads could land a plane.*
So. This is it. The date. Thirty-nine years in the making.

choices.text: Ask him to dance.
Raise a toast to Brenda.
Check your phone.

lines: *He takes your hand. He's warm now. He spins you around the kitchen to 'Livin' on a Prayer.' He is an unbelievably good dancer. Aerobics instructor, after all.*
Halfway there, sweetheart. ...Actually, I think we're all the way there.
To Brenda. Who never got her sink fixed, never got her date and never knew she was the best thing that ever happened to a leak.
*He clinks your glass. It actually clinks.*
And to you. Second best. ...First best. Don't tell Brenda.
*You check your phone. He watches you check your phone.*
Wow. Thirty-nine years I waited for this date and you're checking the group chat.
*He sulks into his wine. Then he steals a meatball off your plate, which he's never been solid enough to do before, so he cheers right up.*
*The candles burn low. Lukey is glowing faintly at the edges, the way people do when they're finally finished with something.*
So. Date's done. Unfinished business... finished. I think I get to choose now. Stay, or go wherever it is leaks go.
What do you reckon, sweetheart?

choices.text: Stay. With me. I'm in love with you, Lukey.
I love you. That's why you should go.
Go. You got your date. You've earned it.
That's your call, Lukey.

lines: *He kisses you. Properly. It's warm and solid and only very slightly damp, for old times' sake.*
Turns out my unfinished business was you, sweetheart. Now it's finished.
...I'm not leaving, though. Obviously. Have you SEEN this hair?

v4_rs2.fxText: The kitchen was completely dry. Nothing else was.
lines: *Much later.*
Best. Date. Ever. Sorry, Brenda.
*He kisses your forehead. Soft. Final.*
Yeah. I love you too. That's how I know. You deserve a fella with a pulse. And a dry floor.
*He gives you one last ridiculous spin, and on the turn he's gone. All that's left is a single drop of water on the floor, shaped exactly like a heart.*
*He gives you a sweaty-headband salute.*
Best frate of my afterlife. Tell the dishwasher he can have the kitchen. He's earned it. Beeping show-off.
*And then he's gone, in a little burst of sparkle and a strong whiff of hairspray.*
*He looks at you for a long time.*
*Then he decides.*
Evening, gorgeous. The dishwasher and I have reached a truce. He beeps, I glare. It's very mature.
*There's a dry, heart-shaped mark on the kitchen floor that no amount of mopping will shift. You've stopped trying.*
*The kitchen smells faintly of hairspray. Somewhere, very quietly, someone is doing the Running Man.*
*Written in the condensation on the kitchen window: 'FIXED IT MYSELF. MOSTLY. YOU HELD THE TORCH. -L x'*
